purpose: Prove that separate AI sessions can repair bounded RCL-owned general compiler builtin-lowering semantics without inheriting K339 self-hosting AI authority.
rules: Each generator receives only mutated compiler candidates, the semantic invariant and observed verifier diagnostics.
Canonical compiler files, mutation implementation and oracle edits are absent from the generator workspace.
Each trial uses a fresh ephemeral read-only session with project rules and user configuration ignored.
The evaluator applies only the exact Schema-bounded edit and requires byte-identical canonical source restoration.
The existing admitted compiler fixed-point receipt may be reused only as runtime evidence; its K339 AI_GENERATE authority is not inherited.
Three unique new sessions plus GitHub focused and Windows replay are required for K327.

trials.intent: Repair contains so the general compiler emits canonical builtin id 1 without changing other text builtins.
Repair sequence_concat so the general compiler emits canonical builtin id 62 without colliding with IR span access.
Repair sha256_text id 70 while preserving unknown builtin fallback id 0.

evidenceBoundary: This proves three bounded independent repairs of compiler builtin lowering plus reuse of the separately admitted compiler fixed point. It grants only K327, not K339, whole-runtime self-hosting, arbitrary compiler evolution or K400 completion.
